title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
The page finishes the previous page's construction and then introduces a nilpotence condition on divided powers, which the next page (§4, Site de De Rham) needs.

(1) Quotient by a sub-PD-ideal. Let (A, J, π) be a ring with a divided-power (PD) ideal, and let x_i ∈ J. The universal PD-morphism (A, J) → (A', J') killing the x_i is the quotient A → A/K. Here K is the ideal generated by all π_n(x_i), n ≥ 1, i.e. the sums Σ λ_{n,i} π_n(x_i) with λ_{n,i} ∈ A. K is the smallest ideal containing the x_i that is stable under all π_n. For an ideal K ⊂ J, the π_n descend to a PD structure on (A/K, J/K) if and only if K is stable under the π_n. In modern terms this is the quotient by a sub-PD-ideal, the PD ideal generated by a set of elements.

(2) A uniform nilpotence condition. A PD ideal is called 'nil-tranquille' if there is an n such that x^{(i)} = 0 for all i ≥ n and all x ∈ J. Since x^{k} = k! x^{(k)}, this gives x^{n+1} = 0 (indeed already x^n = 0). If J is generated by x_1, …, x_N, then J^k is generated by monomials of degree k in the x_j. A monomial of degree ≥ N(n−1)+1 contains some x_j to a power ≥ n, so it vanishes. Hence J^{Nn+1} = 0, the bound written on the page, which is weaker than this.

(3) A pointwise condition. Grothendieck then names the weaker notion 'anneau avec idéal à puissances divisées nilpotentes': for every x there is an n with x^{(i)} = 0 for i ≥ n.

(4) Exponential and logarithm. For such a ring the formal series become finite sums: exp(x) = Σ_{n≥0} x^{(n)} and log(1+x) = Σ_{n≥1} (−1)^{n−1} (n−1)! x^{(n)}. They give mutually inverse group isomorphisms between the multiplicative group 1+J ⊂ A^* and the additive group J. This holds with no denominators, so in any characteristic, e.g. over Z_(p) or Z/p^m.

The page serves §4 (next page): objects of the De Rham (crystalline) site are nilpotent immersions U → U' with a 'tranquil' PD structure on the ideal. The exp/log isomorphism is the standard tool for comparing multiplicative and additive data (e.g. G_m versus G_a, line bundles, Dieudonné theory) on PD thickenings.
errors: Sign of the logarithm: as written (−1)^n (n−1)! x^{(n)} has the wrong sign; it should be (−1)^{n−1} (n−1)! x^{(n)}, since log(1+x) = Σ (−1)^{n−1} x^n/n and x^n/n = (n−1)! x^{(n)}. The summation index for log must start at n = 1.
Minor: from x^{(i)} = 0 for i ≥ n one gets x^n = 0, slightly sharper than the stated x^{n+1} = 0. The bound J^{Nn+1} = 0 is correct but not optimal (N(n−1)+1 suffices).
The 'only if' in (1) implicitly requires K ⊂ J (true here, since the x_i lie in J). The general criterion (Berthelot) concerns K ∩ J being a sub-PD-ideal, or compatibility of the PD structure.

ideas.what: Quotient of a PD ring by the PD ideal generated by elements; the PD structure descends iff the ideal is stable under the π_n
ideas.modern_name: sub-PD-ideal; PD ideal generated by a set; quotient PD structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Roby (1965); Berthelot (Cohomologie cristalline, LNM 407, 1974, Ch. I)
ideas.where_published: Background in Grothendieck's 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968); systematized by Berthelot

ideas.what: Uniformly / pointwise nilpotent divided powers ('nil-tranquille', 'puissances divisées nilpotentes'), with consequence J^{Nn+1}=0 for finitely generated J
ideas.modern_name: PD-nilpotent ideal (J^{[n]}=0) / locally PD-nilpotent; nilpotent divided powers in the crystalline site
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (crystalline site with nilpotent PD, 1966); Berthelot (PD-nilpotence, and removing the nilpotence condition)
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968): crystalline site defined via nilpotent PD thickenings

ideas.what: exp/log isomorphism 1+J ≅ J for a PD-nilpotent ideal, with integral formulas via divided powers
ideas.modern_name: PD exponential/logarithm; truncated exp/log on PD-nilpotent ideals
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; used systematically by Messing (1972), Berthelot–Breen–Messing, Mazur–Messing, Berthelot–Ogus
ideas.where_published: Possibly implicit in Grothendieck, Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné (1970/74); standard in Messing LNM 264

deep.surprise_reason: Standard foundational material on divided powers (sub-PD-ideals, PD-nilpotence, PD exp/log), all well documented in Berthelot, Messing and Berthelot–Ogus. The only point of mild historical interest is the private term 'nil-tranquille / tranquille' for the nilpotence condition imposed on the De Rham site, a terminology choice not a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'nil-triangulaire' / 'triangulaire' should read 'nil-tranquille' / 'tranquille' (consistent with 'puissances divisées tranquilles' on the next page); likewise 'divisées nil-triangulaires' → 'divisées nil-tranquilles'.
'puissance [?] satisfait' is more likely 'qui satisfont' / 'puissances divisées satisfaisant'.
In the log formula the image shows (−1)^n (n−1)! x^{(n)}; the mathematically correct sign is (−1)^{n−1}, and the index should be n ≥ 1.
'nous [?] ... nilpotents, I ... [?]' is roughly 'donc ces éléments nilpotents, J est nilpotent'.
